newsitem.title: USA: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD - Earnings focus, rate worries.
newsitem.headline: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD - Earnings focus, rate worries.

text.p: A flood of quarterly earnings reports will begin this week, while Wall Street wrestles with interest rate worries and braces for a report on consumer prices, analysts said.
They predicted earnings overall would be positive but somewhat lower than the previous quarter.
"We expect overall the larger tech stocks will report reasonably good earnings and most earnings ... will be positive," said Bill Meehan, a market analyst at Prudential Securities.

Tom Carpenter, chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc in Washington, said, "My guess is that ... on a momentum basis fourth-quarter profits will be down slightly on a year-to-year level, although still healthy."
He predicted 1996 yearly profits would rise about 7.5 percent over 1995's, with profits this year up five percent.
John Wosczyna, market strategist at Roney & Co, warned that stock prices could begin to stagnate this week as portfolio managers exhaust pension funds that became available at the start of the year.
"My expectation is that the upside will be completed (this) week and then we go down," he said. "We've had one whale of a bull market for two years."

Banks and financial institutions will begin the earnings parade this week, with NationsBank Corp among those reporting on Monday. The I/B/E/S investment research firm which tracks analysts' estimates said the mean forecast called for NationsBank to report quarterly earnings per share (EPS) of $2.05 against $2.11 for the same period last year.
BankAmerica Corp will release earnings on Wednesday, with I/B/E/S calling for a quarterly EPS of $1.93 against $1.89 for the same period the year before.

Apple Computer Inc will report quarterly earnings on Wednesday after the market's close. The I/B/E/S estimate is for a loss per share of $0.27 against a loss of $0.70 for the same period the year before.
The key economic report due this week is the December consumer price index (CPI), a measure of inflation at the retail level. It is due out Tuesday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

The overall CPI rose 0.3 percent in November, up 0.2 percent excluding volatile food and energy prices. Economists polled by Reuters predicted on average, that Tuesday's report will show overall CPI rose 0.3 percent in December, with an increase of 0.2 percent excluding food and energy items.

The producer price index for December rose only 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. The stock market cheered that news last week with a record close, despite Friday's news of stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs creation.

The jobs report caused a bond market selloff, lifting the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury Bond to 6.85 percent from 6.75 percent on Thursday. The inflation-leery bond market is expected scrutinize the CPI on Tuesday for any signs of price pressures that might convince the Federal Reserve to raise official interest rates.
